why: Design 5's light-gated pacemaker with R as a clean switch: self 7 and bias -6 (on above an input of 3.22, off below 1.78, resting output ~0.025), so R's resting state no longer tilts the wall into an F-R oscillation. With D on, D drives R by 3.43; Q (tau 20, driven 7.5 by R, bias -4) ends a burst after ~8 ticks and lets R fire again only when Q has decayed near its floor (~50 ticks), where a small push from F - SL moves the timing a lot: about 33 ticks after a burst that raised far-field light by B5's margin, never while F < SL. No resting creep: motion comes only from bursts, as B5's from its runs.
